Subject: Walk-up credit ladder proposal for 2028/2029 multi-year

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The exec team liked Redwood’s latency profile and the cost breakdown, and we want to workshop a prepay structure that lets us scale into Q1 2028 without overcommitting in year one. Attached is a short proposal (nimbus_prepay_proposal_v3.pdf) with three options:

1) Flat annual prepay with 10% term discount (year 1,2)
2) Laddered walk-up credits: quarterly triggers that release higher discount brackets as consumption hits thresholds
3) Hybrid bridge + monthly drawdown: smaller upfront wallet + a swingline that bridges to the annual commitment, reconciled monthly

Our preference is #3 — it gives us flexibility early in the contract while protecting Redwood’s unit economics. Questions we had:
- How would the swingline be implemented operationally (invoices, reconciliation cadence)?
- Do you support partial refunds or credit reallocation if we underspend in Q1?
- Are there caps on the discount that would apply for the laddered tiers?

We’ll share expected monthly usage estimates in a follow-up. Can we set a quick call Tues or Wed to align?

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear options in the deck and the preference callout. High level responses below; I copied finance and PM for input on operational flows.

Operational model (swingline + monthly drawdown):
- We can host a small upfront wallet (typically 10–25% of year-1 committed spend) with a swingline facility that allows you to draw beyond the wallet up to an agreed cap.
- Monthly reconciliation: consumption is deducted from the wallet daily and reconciled at month end; if you exceed the wallet we invoice the overage and it pulls from the swingline; if you underconsume we carry the wallet forward for up to 90 days (unless you elect refund).

Refunds / credit reallocation:
- We prefer to avoid cash refunds; standard practice is either carryforward credit or reallocation to a partner project. Refunds can be done but require exec sign-off and a small admin fee.

Discount caps for laddered tiers:
- We typically cap discounts at 25% for any single-year effective rate unless there is a multi‑year guaranteed minimum schedule.

Can Marissa and Karthik confirm tax/invoice flow and the legal redline for a swingline clause? Jordan — I have Wed 10–10:45 AM PT open for a short sync.

—Diego

Diego / team —

Quick operational suggestion based on similar deals: propose a bracketed drawdown ladder with an escrow buffer. Practical points:

- Ladder mechanics: commit to an annual target (A). Wallet is funded at 15% of A up front. Each calendar quarter we evaluate consumption against a cadence. If consumption hits >= 85% of pro-rata run rate for that quarter, the next bracket unlocks a 3–5% incremental discount on additional consumption for that quarter.
- Escrow buffer: Redwood holds a 5% escrow of the wallet value to cover rapid frontloading in month 1–2; escrow is released at the end of Q2 if pacing is met. This reduces our liquidity risk for swingline draws.
- Triggered sweep: if cumulative consumption over a rolling 60-day window overshoots 120% of pro-rata, an automatic sweep converts a portion of the swingline into an invoiceable draw (i.e., prepayment top-up).

Pricing guardrails: max effective discount per year = 22%. If Nimbus wants deeper discounts we require a fixed minimum annual commitment or a multi-year ARR floor.

I can sketch the exact math into the MOP spreadsheet (draft_mop_schedule.xlsx) and run a few consumption scenarios.

—Karthik
